messages:
Maria Gonzales: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we need a final decision on two comms items: statuspage wording for 'degraded performance' vs 'partial outage', and the policy for sharing RCAs with customers. I started an action tracker: https://ourdocs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042/action-tracker :eyes:

incident-bot: Postmortem doc uploaded: https://ourdocs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042/postmortem (owner: @Maria Gonzales) :page_facing_up:

Raj Patel: Thanks Maria. For customers I lean toward more explicit language: call it a "partial outage" if user-facing requests failed >1% for >5min. Otherwise "degraded performance." That threshold keeps SLAs sensible.

Clare Wu: +1 on thresholds. Also action item A3 (retry/backoff improvement) needs an owner assignment — I can take tech lead but need an engineer to implement and a QA signoff.

Maria Gonzales: Clare — can you own A3 tech lead? Who can implement? @Oliver Reed?

Oliver Reed: I can pick up the implementation work. Estimate: 3 dev-days + 1 QA day. Will add to my sprint and link PR.

Raj Patel: For statuspage copy, here's a short draft we can use in the 72h customer summary. Feedback welcome.

Raj Patel: ```We experienced a partial outage impacting API request routing between 02:18–02:44 UTC. Root cause: a misconfigured routing rule in the inference proxy caused a subset of requests to be dropped. Impact: ~2.3% of requests received errors during the window. What we did: rolled back the routing change, reinstated healthy nodes, and validated success criteria. Next steps: improved deploy gating and retry/backoff changes. We will share a full RCA within 72 hours.```

Clare Wu: That reads well. Suggest replacing "we will share a full RCA within 72 hours" with "we will publish the full RCA within 72 hours, and will notify subscribed customers." makes the CTA clearer.

Maria Gonzales: Good call. Also need clarity on who approves external RCA redactions. Our policy currently: redactions require Security + Legal + Incident Owner sign-off. Do we keep that or delegate to Security for low-risk items?

Raj Patel: Recommend: keep the tri-signoff for anything customer-facing. For low-risk operational logs we can let Security approve directly, but we should document exceptions in the tracker.

Oliver Reed: For action owner tracking: I'll add a column "approval_needed" boolean and "approver" list in the tracker. Quick script I use to generate reminders:```#!/bin/bash
# ping owners for overdue actions
curl -s -X POST https://slack.internal/hooks/reminder -d '{"text":"INC-2026-042: action A3 overdue — please update status"}'```

Maria Gonzales: Perfect. Can we also standardize the 72h/30d customer timelines in the incident template? I'll update the postmortem template to include explicit communication deadlines and an explicit field "RCA_sharing_policy: public|restricted|by-consent".

Raj Patel: :thumbsup: If Maria updates the template I'll send the customer comms blurb to legal for quick review — tagging @Legal in the tracker.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: 72h RCA draft due 2026-04-06T14:30:00Z (owner: Maria Gonzales).

Clare Wu: I'll create the PR for the retry/backoff change and link it in the tracker. Putting tentative ETA: 2026-04-05.

Oliver Reed: I'll plan QA for 2026-04-06 and run the canary in staging.

Maria Gonzales: Thanks all. Action items recap (from tracker): A1 statuspage copy — Raj to finalize + Legal review; A2 RCA redaction policy — Maria to update template & doc exceptions; A3 retry/backoff — Clare (tech lead) / Oliver (implement + QA). I'll follow up in 24h with the updated tracker and the finalized statuspage snippet. :sparkles:
